items.title: fix(llm): bound speculative prefill warmup lifetime

labels.name: external-contribution
labels.description: Pull request is from an external contributor

items.body:
Speculative prefill could retain request resources indefinitely when a backend stalled in generation or returned a response stream that never ended. Each preprocessor now owns its warmup tasks and cancels them when dropped. Discovery chat pipelines also inherit their WorkerSet's lifecycle cancellation, so retirement prevents late warmups even when an in-flight request retains the pipeline. After the client response finishes, the asynchronous warmup has a 60-second deadline; cancellation or timeout signals any downstream context and allows up to five seconds of cleanup.

Rendering and tokenization run on the blocking pool, with cancellation checked between operations and before dispatch. A process-wide limit admits at most four speculative preprocessing operations, including work retained by a dropped preprocessor or replaced WorkerSet. Each blocking closure owns its admission permit and remains tracked until it returns. Saturated warmups are skipped without queuing more blocking work. A synchronous operation that has already started cannot be forcibly cancelled; its result cannot dispatch a cancelled warmup.

Regressions cover stalled streams, cooperative cleanup, WorkerSet retirement, and cancellation during preprocessing. Additional cases hold a formatter blocked across owner drop, parent cancellation, and timeout, verify that replacement owners cannot bypass admission, and check that tracking and admission recover only after the closure returns. Pre Merge and full PR CI passed on `7e1bebf81bd`, including all thirteen speculative-prefill tests and the retained-pipeline WorkerSet-retirement regression. Closes #13409.

items.title: Speculative-prefill tasks can wait forever on a stalled backend stream
items.body:
## Description

On current `main` (`13fd4b3fae`), speculative next-turn prefill starts a detached task after the client response reaches `finish_reason`. The task creates an independent `PipelineContext`, calls the next engine, and drains the returned stream until EOF:

- [`maybe_wrap_stream` discards the `JoinHandle`](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/13fd4b3fae/lib/llm/src/preprocessor/speculative_prefill.rs#L95-L108)
- [`prefill_task` drains without a timeout or cancellation branch](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/13fd4b3fae/lib/llm/src/preprocessor/speculative_prefill.rs#L177-L186)

The new context is not linked to the completed client request, and no owner retains a handle with which to stop the task. If the backend returns a stream that remains pending instead of reaching EOF, one task per affected request remains live indefinitely. Each task retains the downstream engine, formatter, tokenizer, copied messages, generated context, response stream, and any guards retained by that stream.

This path is enabled only when `nvext.agent_hints.speculative_prefill` is true, but a stalled backend can then turn completed client requests into an accumulating set of background tasks.

## Expected behavior

Speculative-prefill work should have a bounded lifetime and should stop when its owning runtime shuts down. A stalled warmup stream should not retain a detached task indefinitely.

## Suggested regression test

Use a fake downstream engine that returns a response stream with a permanently pending tail. Drive the wrapped client stream through a response carrying `finish_reason`, then end the owner/runtime and verify through a drop probe that the warmup stream and captured engine are released within a bounded interval.

## Duplicate and overlap check

Semantic searches for speculative prefill, next-turn prefill, `speculative_prefill`, `prefill_task`, stalled streams, timeouts, and task lifetime found no matching issue or pull request. None of the 865 open pull requests changes `lib/llm/src/preprocessor/speculative_prefill.rs`.

items.title: docs: add agent quickstart and surface it from the README
items.body: ## Overview Adds a lightweight **Agent Quickstart** for serving agentic workloads, and makes the existing `docs/agents/` material discoverable from the README front door. The agent-serving features (per-request hints, tracing, priority scheduling) are a headline 1.0 capability, but nothing in the README pointed at the docs — the one "Agentic inference" bullet linked out to LangChain/NeMo, not to our own guides. This closes that gap and gives a copy-paste on-ramp that sits below the full Pi-Mono walkthrough. ## Changes - **`docs/agents/quickstart.md`** (new): curl-only quickstart. Send a normal OpenAI-compatible request, then add `nvext.agent_context` and `nvext.agent_hints` to the same request. No harness or SDK required. Honest about which hints only take effect when the matching feature is enabled, with links to the per-feature pages. Optional tracing step ties into `agent-tracing.md`. - **`docs/agents/README.md`**: add the quickstart as the entry-point row in Core Concepts. - **`docs/index.yml`**: register the quickstart as the first page under the Agents nav section. - **`README.md`**: Quick Start pointer + link in the "New in 1.0" agentic-inference bullet (relative paths). ## Notes - Reuses the exact frontend/worker launch from the README Quick Start (`Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, port 8000); metadata is backend-agnostic. - `pi-mono.md` stays as the full end-to-end harness walkthrough. - All cross-links verified to resolve. --- ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Documentation** * Added comprehensive Agent Quickstart guide with step-by-step instructions for sending agent-aware requests via HTTP, including metadata configuration * Provided guidance on agent context fields, hints (priority, output length, speculative prefill), and optional tracing * Updated documentation navigation and main README to highlight Agent Quickstart resources * Included reference links to related agent configuration and deployment guides

items.title: refactor: extract chat-template rendering into standalone dynamo-renderer crate

labels.name: external-contribution
labels.description: Pull request is from an external contributor

items.body:
## What

Extracts the chat-template / prompt-formatting engine out of `lib/llm` into a new standalone, runtime-free **`dynamo-renderer`** crate, so it can be reused by an external OpenAI frontend (e.g. an SGLang Rust HTTP server) without pulling in the Dynamo runtime.

- New `dynamo-renderer` crate: owns the `OAIChatLikeRequest` trait, HF `chat_template` rendering (minijinja + pycompat), and native DeepSeek formatters (under `deepseek/`). Ships the ready-made impl for `dynamo-protocols`' OpenAI chat request (orphan-rule-legal here since the trait is local). Re-exports `dynamo-tokenizers` as a one-import convenience. Includes `README.md` + `CLAUDE.md` (`AGENTS.md` symlink) matching sibling crates.
- `dynamo-tokenizers` stays a pure tokenization leaf — no protocols, no minijinja, no feature flags.
- `dynamo-protocols` stays a pure wire-types leaf.
- `lib/llm` depends on `dynamo-renderer`; `crate::preprocessor::prompt` keeps only the lib/llm-local glue (`Nv*` impls, the `MediaRequestExt` extension trait, `prompt_formatter_from_mdc`). Everything else imports `dynamo_renderer` directly — no back-compat re-exports. `PromptContextMixin` moves to the crate.

```
dynamo-protocols (wire types, leaf)     dynamo-tokenizers (tokenize, leaf)
                 \                       /
                  dynamo-renderer  (trait + engine + impl; re-exports tokenizers)
                         |
                      dynamo-llm  (Nv* impls, MediaRequestExt, prompt_formatter_from_mdc)
```

## Why a separate crate — and the approach we tried first

The motivating goal was "let an external Rust frontend reuse our chat templating." The first attempt was to **fold the prompt code into `dynamo-tokenizers`** behind a `chat-template` feature — the reasoning being that HF's `apply_chat_template` is a method *on the tokenizer* and the template ships in `tokenizer_config.json`, so it felt conceptually adjacent.

That turned out to be the wrong home, for one concrete reason: **the renderer imports nothing from the tokenizer side of the crate** — it never touches encode/decode/vocab. The only thing binding the two together was the mental model, not the code. The renderer is really a *bridge* between OpenAI request types (`dynamo-protocols`) and the HF jinja engine (`minijinja`).

Forcing it into `dynamo-tokenizers` bought zero code-sharing and created a pile of dependency/feature gymnastics we wanted to avoid:

- **A `tokenizers -> protocols` dependency edge.** The default `OAIChatLikeRequest` impl is for `dynamo_protocols::types::CreateChatCompletionRequest`, and the trait's `typed_messages()` returned a `dynamo_protocols` type. So the "lean leaf" tokenizer crate had to depend (even optionally) on the wire-protocol crate — backwards layering for the most foundational crate, which is also consumed by KV routing / token counting that never touch OpenAI types.
- **A `chat-template` Cargo feature on `dynamo-tokenizers`** (plus `serde_json/preserve_order`, `serde_json/raw_value`, optional `minijinja`/`chrono`/`either`/`dynamo-protocols`) just to keep the default build lean. Feature-gating a whole second persona onto a single-purpose crate.
- **The orphan rule made every alternative awkward.** `impl OAIChatLikeRequest for CreateChatCompletionRequest` can only live in the crate that owns the trait *or* the type. With the trait in tokenizers, that meant either keeping the `tokenizers -> protocols` edge, or inverting it (`protocols` gains a `chat-template` feature that depends on `tokenizers` and hosts the impl) — which then needs a **dev-dependency cycle** so the tokenizer crate's own tests can still construct the protocol type. A third "glue" crate couldn't host the impl at all without a newtype wrapper, which is exactly the wrapper friction external consumers were trying to avoid.

Giving the bridge its own crate dissolves all of it: the trait lives in `dynamo-renderer`, so the protocol impl is local-trait-legal; both leaf crates go back to having a single job and zero feature flags; and dependencies flow one direction only.

## Why "renderer"

The crate is the *encode* half of converting between structured chat (messages + tools) and what the model sees. The natural counterpart is the *decode* half — parsing model output back into reasoning / tool calls — which already lives in `dynamo-parsers`. Naming this `dynamo-renderer` positions it as the encode side of that pairing (cf. the "renderers" concept), leaving room to grow a bidirectional `Renderer` abstraction later that composes render + parse + tokenize.

## Testing

- `dynamo-renderer`: 87 tests. `dynamo-tokenizers`: 37 (lean). `dynamo-llm`: 1137 lib unit + `deepseek_v4`/`v32` integration (12 + 4) pass. clippy + fmt clean across all three.
- Python bindings rebuilt via `maturin develop` against the new crate graph.
- **E2E on 2x L40S** (`dynamo.frontend` + `dynamo.sglang`, Qwen3-0.6B): multi-turn `/no_think` renders correctly (`<think>\n\n</think>\n\nParis.`, finish=stop); tool-calling turn renders the tools section and emits a valid Qwen `<tool_call>` for `get_weather(city=Paris)`.

> Note: `lib/llm/tests/preprocessor.rs` has tests that download the gated `meta-llama/Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct` config and fail with HTTP 401 without an HF token for that repo. Those failures are environmental and reproduce on a clean `main`; the non-gated tests in that file pass.

items.title: feat: speculative prefill [DYN-2166]
items.body:
## Summary

- **Speculative next-turn prefill** — after an assistant turn completes, render the predicted next-turn prefix (history with thinking content stripped) and fire a `max_tokens=1` request to warm the KV cache, gated by `nvext.speculative_prefill`.
- **Reasoning token support in the mocker** — new `--reasoning` CLI flag and `ReasoningConfig` that wraps mocker output in start/end thinking boundary tokens at a configurable ratio.
- **Benchmark improvements** — extract shared utilities into `benches/common/` and add `multiturn_bench` simulating N concurrent multi-turn chat users with TTFT and per-turn latency tracking.

## Test plan

- [x] Run mocker with `--reasoning '{"start_thinking_token_id":..., "end_thinking_token_id":..., "thinking_ratio":0.6}'` and verify thinking boundary tokens appear in output.
- [x] Send a chat completion with `nvext.speculative_prefill: true` and confirm the speculative prefill request fires after the assistant turn completes.
- [x] Verify KV event processing still works end-to-end (store / remove / snapshot) after the channel refactor.
- [x] `cargo bench --bench multiturn_bench --features kv-router-stress -- --ping` smoke test passes.
